claims.claim: One round has the exact form T(p)=reverse(p_i : i in D) followed by (p_i : i not in D), where D={i>=2 : p_i<p_{i-1}} and both subsequences otherwise retain index order.
claims.evidence: The scan marks exactly the descent bottoms. Moving marked indices d_1<...<d_k to the front in that order leaves the front block p_{d_k},...,p_{d_1}; all unmarked elements retain their original relative order. The literal implementation agreed with the formula on every permutation through size 9.
claims.witness: For p=(4,3,1,5,2), D={2,3,5} and both descriptions give T(p)=(2,1,3,4,5).
claims.search_method: Direct operational proof plus exhaustive comparison of literal and closed-form rounds on 409113 permutations.

claims.claim: There is an exact reduction of every maximum-element phase to parallel deletion in a word. Once i+1,...,n are fixed, write the active prefix as L i R. Define A(r_1...r_s)=(r_j : 2<=j<=s and r_{j-1}<r_j). The number of further rounds until i is fixed is h(R)=min{t:A^t(R) is empty}.
claims.evidence: The active maximum i is never marked. The first entry of nonempty R is marked because it follows i, and each later r_j is marked exactly when r_j<r_{j-1}. Hence the entries remaining to the right of i are exactly A(R), independently of L. Iteration gives the claimed extinction time, and every nonempty A-word is strictly shorter. This was exhaustively checked for every active permutation through i=9.
claims.witness: For active prefix (2,5,1,4,3), R=(1,4,3), A(R)=(4), and A^2(R) is empty; exactly two rounds fix 5.
claims.search_method: Symbolic phase analysis, exhaustive active-prefix enumeration, and independent exact verification of the labeled-stack deletion recurrence on every permutation word through length 9.

claims.claim: Let B_0 be empty and B_{m+1}=(m+1)T(B_m). If q(m)=floor((sqrt(8m+1)-1)/2), then h(B_m)=q(m). For m>=2, B_m begins with m and the word to its right also has extinction time q(m).
claims.evidence: The decreasing-stack recurrence assigns each element its exact A-deletion round. Separating the trivial bases, induction with m=q(q+1)/2+r gives the stated consecutive-value stack and label pattern; its maximum label is q. Since B_m=mR_m and m exceeds every entry of R_m, A(B_m)=A(R_m). Both words are nonempty for m>=2, so h(B_m)=1+h(A(B_m))=1+h(A(R_m))=h(R_m). The full claimed stack signature, direct extinction time, and tail equality all agreed for 0<=m<=5000.
claims.witness: B_6=(6,3,1,2,5,4); both B_6 and its tail extinguish in three A-iterations, equal to q(6)=3.
claims.search_method: Inductive invariant audit, direct A-iteration, labeled-stack computation, and exact triangular-number arithmetic.

claims.claim: For i>=2, a phase for active maximum i has its maximum possible length i-1 if and only if its active prefix is exactly (i,1,2,...,i-1).
claims.evidence: Writing the active prefix as L i R gives ell_i=h(R)<=|R|<=i-1. Equality forces L empty and |R|=i-1. Because every nonempty A-iteration deletes its first entry, h(R)=|R| requires the first iteration to delete only that entry, which is equivalent to every adjacent pair of R being increasing. Thus R=(1,...,i-1). Conversely, A repeatedly removes only the first entry of this increasing word, giving i-1 rounds.
claims.witness: The active prefix (5,1,2,3,4) has phase length 4, while exhaustive checking through i=9 found no other prefix attaining i-1.
claims.search_method: Equality-case analysis for both length inequalities plus exhaustive permutation checking through i=9.

claims.claim: If ell_i denotes the phase length for active maximum i, then ell_i+ell_{i-1}<=2i-4 for every i>=5.
claims.evidence: If ell_i<=i-2, combining this with ell_{i-1}<=i-2 proves the bound. Otherwise rigidity gives the phase start (i,1,...,i-1). Induction from the round formula gives T^t=B_t,i,t+1,...,i-1 and endpoint B_{i-1},i, so ell_{i-1}=q(i-1). For i>=5, q(i-1)<=i-3 because q>=i-2 would imply (i-2)(i-1)/2<=i-1 and hence i<=4. Therefore the sum is at most 2i-4.
claims.witness: At i=5, (5,1,2,3,4) has ell_5=4 and ell_4=2, attaining 2i-4=6.
claims.search_method: Complete case split using maximal-phase rigidity and the B-word lemma; exhaustive phase checks on every permutation through n=9.

claims.claim: For n>=5, W(n)<=n(n-1)/2-floor((n-3)/2). Consequently no permutation family requires omega(n^2) rounds.
claims.evidence: The individual phase caps sum to n(n-1)/2. Pairing (n,n-1),(n-2,n-3),... with pair head at least 5 produces exactly floor((n-3)/2) disjoint pairs. Each separate pair cap is 2i-3, whereas claim 4 lowers it to 2i-4, saving one round per pair. The resulting uniform O(n^2) bound precludes omega(n^2) behavior.
claims.witness: For n=5 the bound is 10-1=9, and W(5)=9, so the bound is attained at this boundary.
claims.search_method: Exact phase summation and parity check of the disjoint-pair count, corroborated exhaustively through n=9.

claims.claim: A substantially stronger uniform adjacent-pair bound ell_i+ell_{i-1}<=i+1 is false: for (7,1,2,3,4,5,6), the phases for 7 and 6 have lengths 6 and 3, respectively.
claims.evidence: Exact iteration gives ell_7=6 and then state B_6,7. The tail of the leading 6 in B_6 has extinction time q(6)=3, so ell_6=3. Their sum is 9, exceeding i+1=8.
claims.witness: The concrete counterexample is p=(7,1,2,3,4,5,6), with phase vector including (ell_7,ell_6)=(6,3).
claims.search_method: Literal and closed-form exact simulation of the specified permutation.

claims.claim: For p_n=(n,1,2,...,n-1) and n>=3, at least n-1+floor((sqrt(8(n-1)+1)-1)/2) rounds are required.
claims.evidence: Induction using the exact round map gives T^t(p_n)=B_t,n,t+1,...,n-1 for 0<=t<=n-1. Thus n fixes only after n-1 rounds, at state B_{n-1},n. The following phase for n-1 lasts q(n-1) rounds by claim 2, proving the lower bound. Exact checks confirmed both phase lengths for every 3<=n<=500.
claims.witness: For n=3, p_3=(3,1,2) requires 3 rounds, exactly 2+q(2)=3.
claims.search_method: Induction on the special-state orbit plus exact simulation through n=500.

claims.claim: Under the zero-no-op-round convention, the exact worst-case values for n=1,...,9 are 0,1,3,6,9,12,18,21,26.
claims.evidence: Complete enumeration of all sum_{n=1}^9 n!=409113 permutations using both the literal marked-move implementation and the independently checked closed round map reproduced exactly 0,1,3,6,9,12,18,21,26. Exhaustion supplies both lower witnesses and matching upper bounds.
claims.witness: For n=9, (3,9,4,5,1,2,6,7,8) requires 26 rounds; maximizers were also found for every smaller n.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive exact enumeration of every permutation for each size 1 through 9.

target_evidence: The draft rigorously rules out omega(n^2) rounds and slightly improves the universal quadratic bound, while also establishing structural phase results, a lower-bound family, and exact small values. It does not determine the asymptotically tight order: the displayed family gives only a linear-order lower bound, leaving a linear-to-quadratic gap. Its explicit PARTIAL resolution label is therefore accurate.
